If DC/WB had made "Batman v Superman" being nothing except four hours of deposition video in the "Wayne Enterprises v. John Doe a.k.a. The Superman" civil lawsuit that would have followed from what happened in MoS, then it would have been a substantially more interesting movie than what we got.

Story: 5/10. I didn't buy it. Yes, the movie centers on Bruce's animosity for Superman as well as perceiving him as a threat. So then Bruce suddenly wants to kill Supes like a maniacal Lex? Same with Lex wanting to kill Supes. It is clearly established in Bruce Timm's DC Universe why Lex hates Supes, but for the average moviegoer, he just sees Lex wanting to kill Supes for the hell of it. Wonder Woman appearing in the movie just seemed forced.

Characters & Acting: 4/10. Eisenberg as Lex was just horrible. When they picked him for Lex a few years ago, I said it was going to be like a young Woody Allen playing Lex. I've seen him in plenty of movies, and he's always playing the same neurotic, stuttering Jew kid. People were telling me he played a great Facebook Zuckerberg. You mean Eisenberg - a stuttering, stammering Woody Allen type - playing a Jewish Zuckerberg required Eisenberg to even act instead of just being himself? Really? Samuel L. Jackson playing Lex would have been far more convincing despite him being black. Then Gadot's forced scenes. You would think she would have all eyes on her when she walks into the room (or on the screen), but she has no impact whatsoever. She is just...there. You never think of her as Wonder Woman even when she is wearing the Wonder Woman outfit. I really don't know how she's going to carry the solo Wonder Woman movie by herself. I still detect her Yiddish accent which is a bit distracting. Cavill is the same. Not much prescence. Affleck is he only character with feeling where you can relate to and attach yourself emotionally to.

Special Effects: 4/10. WTF with the Lord of the Rings cave troll? I was expecting Legolas to climb on his head and shoot an arrow into his skull. Terrible CGI for a $200+ million film budget. For a 2.5 hour movie, you would think they would throw in more than once car chase scene and one Bat vs. Supes scene.

Overall: 5/10. I may be biased because I've watched and followed all of Bruce Timm's DC animated work: Superman: The Animated Series, Batman: TAS, Justice League, Justice League Unlimited. I have seen every DC Universe animated movie to date (over 20 of them). So seeing Snyder take his liberties with Lex Luthor by having some fucking dweeb play him was not going to win me over. Gadot as Wonder Woman would probably have annoyed me too except she wasn't on screen long enough for me to hate her like Eisenberg.

i just got back from seeing batman vs. superman: dawn of justice sunday night and i really enjoyed this movie. of the dc movies i've seen i'd rank it third best after the first two nolan batman movies and in front of snyder's superman movie. i liked aflek as the batman much more than i expeted to.

i have a couple of issus with the film. the first was that some of the transitions seemed abrupt to me. i don't know if they were an editing issue or a story issue but there were several times where it was noticible to the point that it took me took me out of the movie. perhaps some of the scenes that were cut out might make these transitions smother.

the second issue i have is the scope of the story- there were too many different storylines for one movie. the conflict between bats and the big blue cheese has a lot of room for a full length movie as does the doomsday story and the formation of the justice league. i think any one of these story lines would have resulted in a better more focused movie than trying to get all three of them into one. in fact i think my issues with jumpy transitions may have had to do with trying to shoe horn all three story lines together.

(as an asside i think this was the major problem with nolan's last batman film too. batman vs. bane or batman returning from retirement would've been plenty of story for a single movie.)

the last thing is that although i didn't hate eisenberg as luthor i thought he came accross as much too young. he even seemed more youthful than the lex from the wb tv series which was a little weird. he just didn't ever seem to have any presence to him which was unfortunate.
